### Observed differences

- A09 and A16 exchanged their occurrence roles. In the earlier window A09 ran in every case, about twice per case, and repeated in about 48 in 100 cases, while A16 ran once in about 50 in 100 cases; in the later window A09 runs once in about 49 in 100 cases and never repeats, while A16 runs in every case, about 1.9 times per case, repeating in about 44 in 100 cases. [OCC001, OCC002]
- Their sequence positions swapped accordingly: A09's median relative position fell from about 0.86 to about 0.47 of the case, while A16's rose from about 0.40 to about 0.86. [POS001, POS002]
- The neighbouring activities rewired around them. A04 and A10 sent all of their observed outgoing transitions to A09 before and all to A16 after; A01 and A13 redirected from A16 (about 20 and 23 in 100 of their outgoing transitions) to A09 (about 18 and 27 in 100). A09's successors changed from A05, A14 and A06 (about 25, 24 and 50 in 100) to A01, A04, A10 and A13, while A16's changed from A13, A10, A04 and A01 to A05, A06 and A14 (about 24, 54 and 22 in 100) — the two successor sets exchanged almost one-for-one. [DIR002, DIR004, DIR001, DIR005, DIR003, DIR006]
- Pairwise distances mirrored the exchange, with support counts swapping too: A09 followed A06 immediately before (gap 1 in all 200 supporting traces) and A16 does now (gap 1 in all 200); A16 reached A10 within 1–3 steps in 54 traces before versus A09 within 1–3 in 54 after; A16 reached A04 closely before (46 traces) versus A09 closely after (43); A13 reached A16 within 1–2 steps before (74 traces) versus A09 within 1–2 after (79); A01 reached A16 within 1–2 before (75 traces) versus A09 within 1–2 after (72). [LAG005, LAG012, LAG013, LAG006, LAG010, LAG003, LAG009, LAG008, LAG002, LAG001]
- Relation shares agree with the same picture: A04 before A09 (about 28 in 100 traces) gave way to A09 before A04 (about 23 in 100); A06 now co-occurs with A16 in every case and follows it (about 56 in 100 strictly after, the rest interleaved through A16's repetitions); A01 and A06, which always co-occurred with A09, now appear without it in about half of the cases; A05, previously seen only together with A09 (about 39 in 100 cases), now appears only together with A16 (same share); A09–A14 co-occurrence fell from about 42 to about 17 in 100 traces. [REL003, REL008, REL001, REL005, REL011]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that A09 and A16 exchanged places in the process flow, each taking over the other's occurrence pattern, repetition behaviour and neighbours. In the later window, A16 occupies the position A09 held before — mandatory, about 1.9 runs per case with repetitions in about 44 in 100 cases, late in the case, preceded by A04 and A10, and leading to A05, A06 and A14 — while A09 occupies A16's former position — a single run in about half of the cases, earlier in the case, preceded by A13 and A01, and leading to A01, A04, A10 and A13. The exchange is shown directly by the rewiring of predecessors and successor sets and by the mirrored pairwise distances, whose support counts also swap; the occurrence, position and relation items all point the same way. With 39 qualifying items against roughly 0.39 expected by chance for the control-flow family, and every item's difference larger than in about 995 of 1,000 random re-splits, sampling variation cannot account for the pattern as a whole. Limitations: positions and gaps are counted in event positions, not clock time, so the exchange concerns placement in the case sequence; and the evidence cannot rule out that the two windows mix different pre-existing process variants rather than reflecting one modified flow, nor that A16's new repetitions serve a different purpose than A09's former ones. [OCC001, OCC002, POS001, POS002, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG005, LAG006, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010, LAG012, LAG013, REL003, REL005, REL008]

Other differences: Small redistributions accompany the exchange — A13's outgoing share to A15 rose from about 21 to 26 in 100 while its share to A01 fell from about 35 to 28, and A01's share to A04 rose slightly — consistent with the same rewiring rather than a separate change. [DIR005, DIR001]
